specs.anchorText: This section opens the restoration chapter by studying the damage itself.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a friendly cartoon repair-shop worker (a cheerful person in an apron, inclusive and approachable) standing at a tidy workbench, holding a damaged photograph that is visibly blurry, speckled with grainy noise dots, and has a small torn hole in one corner. On the workbench sit three small labeled tools arranged in order: a magnifying glass, a tiny rule book, and a screwdriver, suggesting a three-step recipe. A clean restored photo glows gently on a small easel beside the worker. The mood is calm and confident, like a watch repairer about to fix something delicate. Style friendly and flat-vector, like an XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt textbook illustration, minimal clutter, one clear scene. No text or lettering in the image except possibly one or two very short faint labels. Gentle, immediately understandable humor.
specs.alt: A friendly cartoon repair-shop worker at a workbench holds a blurry, noisy, torn photograph while a cleanly restored photo glows on an easel nearby, with three small tools (magnifier, rule book, screwdriver) laid out in order, depicting restoration as the disciplined craft of modeling damage, naming a prior, and inverting it to recover a clean image.
specs.caption: Restoration is not magic, it is patient repair: figure out how the photo got damaged, decide what a clean photo should look like, then carefully undo the harm.

specs.anchorText: Figure 7.1.1 traces the full journey from scene to file
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a gentle conveyor-belt assembly line where a crisp, happy little landscape photo enters on the left and travels through four cartoon machine stations, getting slightly more damaged at each one. Station one (a lens machine) smears it soft and blurry. Station two (a sensor machine) sprinkles it with tiny grainy dots. Station three (an electronics machine with little sparks) adds faint static. Station four (a boxy compression machine) stamps a faint blocky grid pattern on it. The photo emerges on the right looking tired and damaged. Above, a small dashed reverse arrow loops back, hinting that restoration runs the line backward. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive but simple machines with cartoon eyes, minimal clutter, one clear left-to-right flow. No text or lettering in the image except at most a few very short faint labels.
specs.alt: A cartoon conveyor belt carries a clean photo through four damage stations (lens blur, sensor grain, electronics static, compression blocking), each adding a characteristic flaw, with a dashed reverse arrow looping back, depicting the degradation pipeline that turns an ideal scene into a damaged observed image and restoration as running that pipeline in reverse.
specs.caption: Every photo rolls off a little assembly line of damage, and you can only run that line backward if you know what each machine did to it.

specs.anchorText: non-local means (NLM) asks "who, anywhere, is living the same life."
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a brick wall scene where one highlighted brick (with a friendly cartoon face) is happily comparing notes with several other look-alike bricks scattered across the wall, connected to them by gentle glowing green threads of friendship, no matter how far apart they sit. Meanwhile a nearby brick that sits on the other side of a dark mortar edge looks different and is politely turned away, connected by a faint dashed red thread that fades out. The idea is that the central brick trusts its true look-alikes anywhere in the image rather than just its physical neighbors. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive cartoon brick characters, minimal clutter, one clear visual metaphor. No text or lettering in the image except at most one or two very short faint labels.
specs.alt: A highlighted cartoon brick on a wall connects with glowing green threads to several similar-looking bricks scattered far across the wall, while politely rejecting a nearby but different brick across an edge with a faded dashed thread, depicting non-local means denoising as averaging a pixel only with patches that genuinely resemble it from anywhere in the image.
specs.caption: A noisy pixel trusts its look-alikes from anywhere in the image, not just the strangers who happen to live next door.

specs.anchorText: the entire craft lies in refusing to divide where the divisor is tiny
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a cautious cartoon hiker character (representing a careful filter) walking along a path of stepping stones over a series of deep canyon gaps. Where the stones are solid and high, the hiker strides confidently. But at spots where the stones shrink to almost nothing over a bottomless gap, the hiker wisely stops and steps gently aside instead of leaping, while a reckless shadow-twin who tries to jump across one of those tiny stones goes flying upward in a comic explosion of noise specks. The contrast shows a careful traveler refusing to cross where the footing is too small. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive characters, minimal clutter, one clear visual metaphor. No text or lettering in the image except at most one or two very short faint labels.
specs.alt: A careful cartoon hiker crosses a canyon on stepping stones, striding over solid high stones but wisely stepping aside where the stones shrink to almost nothing, while a reckless twin who leaps onto a tiny stone is flung skyward in a burst of noise specks, depicting the Wiener filter recovering frequencies where signal is strong but refusing to divide where the blur has crushed them near zero.
specs.caption: Dividing by a frequency the blur nearly erased is how a whisper of noise becomes a scream; the smart filter simply refuses to make that jump.

specs.anchorText: The craft is reading the hole, what structures it interrupts and how wide it is
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: three friendly little cartoon helper characters each fixing the same kind of hole in a picture, side by side as three gentle vignettes. The first helper, holding a paint roller, smoothly blends color inward across a small hole leaving a soft gradient. The second helper, holding a pencil, carefully extends an interrupted line straight across a hole so the edge continues. The third helper, holding a copy-stamp tool, lifts a patch of brick texture from elsewhere in the image and presses it neatly into a textured hole. Each helper has a distinct, complementary job. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive simple characters, minimal clutter, three clear panels of one consistent metaphor. No text or lettering in the image except at most a few very short faint labels.
specs.alt: Three friendly cartoon helpers fix holes in a picture three different ways: one smoothly blends color inward with a roller, one extends an interrupted line across the gap with a pencil, and one copies brick texture from elsewhere with a stamp tool, depicting smoothness, structure-continuing, and exemplar inpainting as different priors suited to different holes.
specs.caption: There is no single way to fill a hole: read what the gap interrupts, then pick the helper who can actually bridge it, smoothing, continuing a line, or copying texture.

specs.anchorText: multi-frame super-resolution collects information you did not have
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: on the left, one lonely blurry photo of a small house stands alone with a confused shrug, labeled as a single witness who only has a rumor. On the right, several slightly-shifted copies of the same blurry house photo are gently sliding and stacking together onto a finer grid, and where they overlap a crisp, sharp, high-resolution house emerges in the middle. The visual idea is that many slightly offset blurry views combine into one genuinely sharper picture. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive but simple, a faint grid showing the samples interleaving, minimal clutter, one clear before-and-after metaphor. No text or lettering in the image except at most one or two very short faint labels.
specs.alt: On the left a single blurry photo of a house shrugs alone; on the right several slightly shifted blurry copies of the same house slide and stack onto a finer grid, and where they overlap a crisp sharp house emerges, depicting multi-frame super-resolution fusing sub-pixel-shifted low-resolution frames into genuine new detail that no single frame contains.
specs.caption: One blurry frame is a rumor, but several slightly shifted frames are sworn testimony: stack their sub-pixel views and real detail no single shot held comes into focus.

specs.anchorText: produce the halos and radioactive "HDR look" that gave the term a bad name
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm, soft palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a cartoon tone-mapping chef character standing proudly over a photo of a room with a window, but the chef has cranked a big dial far past a sensible mark, and the resulting image looks comically overcooked: a glowing halo ring around the window frame, an unnaturally grayish dramatic sky, and an over-saturated, slightly radioactive-looking interior. Beside it, a small, calm, natural-looking version of the same photo waits with a gentle thumbs up, showing the tasteful alternative. The humor is the over-eager chef ruining a good measurement with too much processing. Friendly flat-vector textbook style, expressive characters, minimal clutter, one clear contrast. No text or lettering in the image except at most one or two very short faint labels.
specs.alt: A cartoon tone-mapping chef cranks a dial far past a sensible mark and proudly presents an overcooked HDR photo with a glowing halo around the window, a grayish dramatic sky, and an over-saturated interior, while a calm natural version of the same photo waits beside it, depicting how aggressive local tone mapping produces the halos and radioactive HDR look that overspends the radiance measurement.
specs.caption: Push tone mapping too hard and you trade a faithful radiance measurement for halos and a radioactive glow; restraint, not the maxed-out dial, is what looks natural.
